package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						sourceCount++;
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot be on the edge");
						}
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						Coordinate targetCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
						if (isWithinBounds(targetCoord) && cells[targetCoord.row][targetCoord.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
						}
						foundSource = termCell;
					} else if (termCell.isSink()) {
						sinkCount++;
						if (!(r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be on the edge");
						}
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						Coordinate targetCoord = new Coordinate(r, c).add(dir.getOffset());
						if (isWithinBounds(targetCoord)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
						foundSink = termCell;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Exactly one source cell required");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Exactly one sink cell required");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (!(targetCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell fillable = (FillableCell) targetCell;
		if (fillable.isOccupied()) {
			return false;
		}
		fillable.setPipe(p);
		return true;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		int row = coord.row;
		int col = coord.col;
		if (!isWithinBounds(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of bounds");
		}
		Cell currentCell = cells[row][col];
		if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not fillable");
		}
		cells[row][col] = new FillableCell();
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (sourceCell == null || cells == null || rows == 0 || cols == 0) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<CoordinateDistance> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
		queue.add(new CoordinateDistance(sourceCell.getCoordinate(), 0));
		filledTiles.add(sourceCell.getCoordinate());
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			CoordinateDistance current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = current.distance;
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (isWithinBounds(neighbor) && !filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
					if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
						((FillableCell) cell).setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						queue.add(new CoordinateDistance(neighbor, currentDist + 1));
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoordinate();
		queue.add(start);
		visited.add(start);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.getCoordinate())) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell || currentCell instanceof Pipe) {
				for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
					Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
					if (!isWithinBounds(neighbor) || visited.contains(neighbor)) {
						continue;
					}
					Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
					if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell || neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
						boolean canEnter = false;
						if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
							TerminationCell sink = (TerminationCell) neighborCell;
							if (neighbor.equals(sink.getCoordinate()) && sink.getDirection() == dir.getOpposite()) {
								canEnter = true;
							}
						} else if (neighborCell instanceof Pipe) {
							Pipe pipe = (Pipe) neighborCell;
							if (pipe.allowsEntryFrom(dir.getOpposite())) {
								if (pipe.allowsExitTo(dir)) {
									canEnter = true;
								}
							}
						}
						if (canEnter) {
							visited.add(neighbor);
							queue.add(neighbor);
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

public class Map {
    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    // Existing constructors...

    /**
     * Constructor that initializes an empty map with given rows and columns.
     * All cells are initialized as FillableCell.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
            }
        }
        // Initialize source and sink cells as needed, or leave null if not applicable
        this.sourceCell = null;
        this.sinkCell = null;
    }
}

Response Text:---
The core issue is that the `Map` class does not have a constructor with the signature `Map(int, int)` or `Map(int, int, Cell[][])`, which the tests and code are attempting to invoke. To fix this, you need to define a constructor in the `Map` class that accepts `int rows, int cols` and initializes the `cells` array accordingly, also setting `sourceCell` and `sinkCell` to null if not provided.

Here's a correct implementation of the `Map` class with the necessary constructor:

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {
    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;
    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    /**
     * Constructor that initializes an empty map with given rows and columns.
     * All cells are initialized as FillableCell.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
            }
        }
        this.sourceCell = null;
        this.sinkCell = null;
    }

    /**
     * Constructor that initializes the map with specified cells.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
        }
        this.sourceCell = null;
        this.sinkCell = null;
    }

    // Existing methods...
}
```

**Explanation:**  
- The constructor `public Map(int rows, int cols)` creates a new map with all cells as `FillableCell`.  
- The constructor `public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells)` allows initializing the map with a predefined cell layout, which is used in tests and other parts of the code.  
- This resolves the compilation errors caused by missing constructors, ensuring the tests and code invoking these constructors will compile and run successfully.

Response Text:---
The `getConnections()` method should determine the directions in which the pipe connects based on its shape. Typically, a pipe's shape defines its connection points: for example, a horizontal pipe connects left and right, a vertical connects up and down, and a cross connects all four directions. The method should throw an `IllegalStateException` if the shape is unrecognized.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public Direction[] getConnections() {
    switch (shape) {
        case HORIZONTAL:
            return new Direction[] {Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
        case VERTICAL:
            return new Direction[] {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN};
        case TOP_LEFT:
            return new Direction[] {Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT};
        case TOP_RIGHT:

- Retrieve the list of players from `configuration.getPlayers()`.
- Cycle through players in order, allowing each to make a move via `nextMove()`.
- Update the game state with each move, refresh the output, and check for a winner after each move.
- Exit the loop when a winner is found, returning the winner.

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int currentIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        Player currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
        this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;

        // Get available moves for current player
        Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
        if (moves.length == 0) {
            // No moves available, skip turn or handle as per game rules
            // For simplicity, assume game continues
            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
            continue;
        }

        // Retrieve the player's next move
        Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);

        // Make the move
        movePiece(move);

        // Update score if needed (assuming last move info is available)
        // For demonstration, suppose last move info is stored or passed
        // Here, we can call updateScore if applicable
        // updateScore(currentPlayer, move.getPiece(), move);

        // Refresh output after move
        this.refreshOutput();

        // Check for winner
        winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, move.getPiece(), move);
        if (winner != null) {
            break;
        }

        // Prepare for next turn
        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
        this.numMoves++;
    }

    System.out.println();
    System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
    System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
    return winner;
}
```

- Initializes game state and retrieves players.
- Loops infinitely, cycling through players.
- For each player:
  - Gets available moves.

  - Executes the move with `movePiece()`.
  - Refreshes the game display.
  - Checks for a winner with `getWinner()`.
- Breaks the loop when a winner is found and returns the winner.

This implementation ensures the game proceeds turn-by-turn, respecting the order in `Configuration#getPlayers()`, and terminates correctly when a winner emerges.

Response Text:---
The `getWinner` method should determine if the last move resulted in a winning condition. Typically, in games like this, a player wins when they meet certain criteria, such as controlling a specific number of pieces, reaching a goal, or occupying specific positions. Since the code context does not specify the exact winning condition, a common approach is to check if the last move resulted in the last player having no remaining pieces or reaching a specific goal.

Assuming the game involves players moving pieces on a board, a typical winning condition could be: if the last move caused the opponent to have no remaining pieces, then the last player wins.

Here's a brief explanation:
- The method checks the current state of the board after the last move.
- It verifies if the opponent has any remaining pieces.
- If the opponent has no pieces left, the last player is declared the winner.
- Otherwise, it returns null, indicating no winner yet.

Below is a complete implementation based on this common logic:

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Determine the opponent player
    Player opponent = null;
    for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
        if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            opponent = player;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (opponent == null) {
        return null; // No opponent found, unlikely scenario
    }

    // Check if the opponent has any remaining pieces on the board
    boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
                opponentHasPieces = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponentHasPieces) {
            break;
        }
    }

    // If opponent has no pieces left, lastPlayer wins
    if (!opponentHasPieces) {
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // No winner yet
    return null;
}
```

This implementation assumes:
- The `board` is a 2D array of `Piece` objects.
- Each `Piece` has a method `getOwner()` returning the `Player` who owns it.
- The game ends when one player has no remaining pieces.

Adjust the winning condition as needed based on the specific rules of your game.

@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Determine the opponent player
    Player opponent = null;
    for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
        if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            opponent = player;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (opponent == null) {
        return null; // No opponent found, unlikely scenario
    }

    // Check if the opponent has any remaining pieces on the board
    boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
                opponentHasPieces = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponentHasPieces) {
            break;
        }
    }

    // If opponent has no pieces left, lastPlayer wins
    if (!opponentHasPieces) {
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // No winner yet
    return null;

Response Text:---
The `updateScore` method calculates the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination places and adds this value to the player's current score. This aligns with the description that each move's score is based on the Manhattan distance, and the player's total score is cumulative.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
    int currentScore = player.getScore();
    player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
}
```

Response Text:---
The `movePiece` method should perform the following steps:
1. Retrieve the source and destination `Place` objects from the `Move`.
2. Use the coordinates of these places to access the corresponding `Piece` objects in the `board` array.
3. Move the `Piece` from the source position to the destination position.
4. Set the source position to `null` to indicate the piece has moved away.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public void movePiece(Move move) {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();

    int sourceX = source.x();
    int sourceY = source.y();
    int destX = destination.x();
    int destY = destination.y();

    // Retrieve the piece from the source position
    Piece movingPiece = board[sourceX][sourceY];

    // Move the piece to the destination position
    board[destX][destY] = movingPiece;

    // Remove the piece from the source position
    board[sourceX][sourceY] = null;
}

The method `getAvailableMoves` needs to iterate over all pieces belonging to the specified player on the board, retrieve each piece's available moves via `Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)`, and collect only the valid moves into a list, which is then returned as an array.

Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    // Verify move validity if necessary (e.g., not moving onto own piece)
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    Piece destPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];
                    if (destPiece == null || !destPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

- Loop through the entire board.
- For each piece belonging to the given player, get its available moves.
- For each move, check if the destination is either empty or occupied by an opponent's piece, ensuring move validity.
- Collect all valid moves into a list and return as an array.

This implementation ensures all returned moves are valid according to the game's rules.

				break;
			}

		}

		System.out.println("Congratulations! ");

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
			if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = player;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
					opponentHasPieces = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentHasPieces) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!opponentHasPieces) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		int sourceX = source.x();
		int sourceY = source.y();
		int destX = destination.x();
		int destY = destination.y();
		Piece movingPiece = board[sourceX][sourceY];
		board[destX][destY] = movingPiece;
		board[sourceX][sourceY] = null;
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			Player currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
			this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
				currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
				continue;
			}
			Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, move.getPiece(), move);
			if (winner != null) {
				break;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
			this.numMoves++;
		}
		System.out.println();
		System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
		System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
		return winner;
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
			if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = player;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
					opponentHasPieces = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentHasPieces) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!opponentHasPieces) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		int sourceX = source.x();
		int sourceY = source.y();
		int destX = destination.x();
		int destY = destination.y();
		Piece movingPiece = board[sourceX][sourceY];
		board[destX][destY] = movingPiece;
		board[sourceX][sourceY] = null;
	}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    // Verify move validity if necessary (e.g., not moving onto own piece)
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    Piece destPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];
                    if (destPiece == null || !destPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

The compilation errors indicate that the `Move` class does not have a `getPiece()` method, and the `Piece` class does not have a `getOwner()` method. To fix these issues, you should replace calls to `move.getPiece()` with `move.getSource()` to get the starting `Place`, and then retrieve the `Piece` from the `board` array using that `Place`. Similarly, replace `piece.getOwner()` with `piece.getPlayer()` if `getPlayer()` is the correct method to obtain the owner of a `Piece`. 

Here's the corrected method implementation:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    Piece destPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];
                    if (destPiece == null || !destPiece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Note:** Ensure that `Piece` has a method `getPlayer()` to retrieve its owner, and that `Move` has methods `getDestination()` and `getSource()` returning `Place` objects. If your classes use different method names, adjust accordingly.

	 * Get all available moves of one player.

	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>

	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {

		return new Move[0];

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			Player currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
			this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
				currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
				continue;
			}
			Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, move.getPiece(), move);
			if (winner != null) {
				break;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.length;
			this.numMoves++;
		}
		System.out.println();
		System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
		System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
		return winner;
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
			if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = player;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)) {
					opponentHasPieces = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentHasPieces) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (!opponentHasPieces) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int currentScore = player.getScore();
		player.setScore(currentScore + distance);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		int sourceX = source.x();
		int sourceY = source.y();
		int destX = destination.x();
		int destY = destination.y();
		Piece movingPiece = board[sourceX][sourceY];
		board[destX][destY] = movingPiece;
		board[sourceX][sourceY] = null;
	}
}

- BOT: 
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    // Verify move validity if necessary (e.g., not moving onto own piece)
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    Piece destPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];
                    if (destPiece == null || !destPiece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

Response Text:---
The compilation errors indicate that the `Move` class does not have a `getPiece()` method, and the `Piece` class does not have a `getOwner()` method. To fix these issues, you should replace calls to `move.getPiece()` with `move.getSource()` (which returns a `Place`), and then retrieve the `Piece` from the board at that position. Similarly, replace `piece.getOwner()` with `piece.getPlayer()` if `getPlayer()` is the correct method to get the owner of a piece.

Here's the corrected method for `getAvailableMoves`:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place currentPlace = new Place(x, y);
                for (Move move : piece.getAvailableMoves(this, currentPlace)) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    Piece destPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];
                    if (destPiece == null || !destPiece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

And for the `getWinner` method, replace `piece.getOwner()` with `piece.getPlayer()`:

```java
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    Player opponent = null;
    for (Player player : configuration.getPlayers()) {
        if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            opponent = player;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (opponent == null) {
        return null;
    }
    boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(opponent)) {
                opponentHasPieces = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponentHasPieces) {
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!opponentHasPieces) {
        return lastPlayer;
    }
    return null;
}
```

**Brief explanation:**  
The errors are caused by attempting to call `getPiece()` and `getOwner()` methods on `Move` and `Piece` objects, respectively, which do not exist. The correct approach is to access the source position of the move, retrieve the piece from the board at that position, and then use `getPlayer()` to identify the owner. This aligns with the existing class design and resolves the compilation errors.

To align with the instructions and ensure the user player moves first, the current implementation is appropriate because the user player is placed first in the players array.

Here's a brief explanation:
- Creates `ConsolePlayer` for the user and `RandomPlayer` for the computer.
- Constructs a `Configuration` with these players, the specified size, and move protection.
- Adds initial `Knight` pieces for each player at specified positions.
- Returns a new `JesonMor` game initialized with this configuration.

Below is the complete method implementation:

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    // Create players: user and computer
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    // Initialize configuration with user first to ensure user moves first
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);
    // Create initial pieces for each player
    Knight knight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    Knight knight2 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    // Place the user's knight at position (0,0)
    configuration.addInitialPiece(knight1, 0, 0);
    // Place the computer's knight at position (1,0)
    configuration.addInitialPiece(knight2, 1, 0);
    // Create and return the game instance
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This implementation ensures the game is properly initialized with the user player moving first, initial pieces placed, and the game object returned successfully.

public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {

        {1, 2},

        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

        if (validateMove(game, move)) {

        }

The task is to implement the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` class, which moves similarly to a cannon in Xiangqi. The Archer can move any number of empty squares along ranks or files, but capturing requires jumping over exactly one piece (the "screen") in the same line.

**Approach:**
1. Identify all possible moves along the four directions (up, down, left, right).
2. For each direction:
   - Traverse squares until hitting the boundary or an occupied square.
   - For non-capturing moves: move through empty squares until blocked.
   - For capturing moves: after passing over exactly one piece (the screen), if the next occupied square contains an opponent's piece, add that move.
3. Validate each move with `validateMove`.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = { {0, 1}, {0, -1}, {1, 0}, {-1, 0} }; // right, left, down, up
    int maxRows = game.getConfiguration().getBoardRows();
    int maxCols = game.getConfiguration().getBoardCols();

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        boolean screenFound = false;
        int row = source.getRow() + dir[0];
        int col = source.getCol() + dir[1];

        while (row >= 0 && row < maxRows && col >= 0 && col < maxCols) {
            Place targetPlace = new Place(row, col);
            Piece targetPiece = game.getPieceAt(targetPlace);

            if (!screenFound) {
                // Moving through empty squares or capturing without jumping
                if (targetPiece == null) {
                    // Empty square, valid move
                    Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                } else {
                    // Found a screen piece, need to jump over it
                    screenFound = true;
                }
            } else {
                // After screen is found, look for opponent's piece to capture
                if (targetPiece != null) {
                    // Can only capture opponent's piece
                    if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    // Stop after attempting capture
                    break;
                }
                // If empty, continue searching
            }
            row += dir[0];
            col += dir[1];
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation:**
- The method iterates over four directions.
- It moves step-by-step along each direction.
- Initially, it adds all empty squares as valid moves.
- When it encounters the first piece, it marks `screenFound = true`.
- After the screen, it looks for an opponent's piece to capture.
- All moves are validated with `validateMove` before adding.

This implementation ensures all valid moves for the Archer are correctly generated, considering the rules of movement and capturing in Xiangqi.

	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] directions = { {0, 1}, {0, -1}, {1, 0}, {-1, 0} }; // right, left, down, up

public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check whether the move for an Archer piece follows the movement rules similar to a cannon in Chinese chess. Specifically, an Archer can move any number of empty squares along a rank or file, but to capture, it must jump over exactly one piece (the "screen") and land on an opponent's piece.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int targetRow = move.getTarget().getRow();
    int targetCol = move.getTarget().getCol();

    // Check if move is along a straight line
    if (sourceRow != targetRow && sourceCol != targetCol) {
        return false; // Not a straight line move
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (sourceRow == targetRow) {
        // Moving horizontally
        int start = Math.min(sourceCol, targetCol) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(sourceCol, targetCol);
        for (int col = start; col < end; col++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withCol(col)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Moving vertically
        int start = Math.min(sourceRow, targetRow) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(sourceRow, targetRow);
        for (int row = start; row < end; row++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withRow(row)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    // Destination piece
    boolean isCapture = game.getPiece(move.getTarget()) != null;

    if (isCapture) {
        // To capture, exactly one piece must be between source and target
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // To move without capturing, no pieces should be between source and target
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}
```

**Note:** This implementation assumes that `move.getSource()` and `move.getTarget()` return objects with `getRow()` and `getCol()` methods, and that `game.getPiece(Position)` returns the piece at a position or null if empty. Adjust accordingly if your classes differ.

    }

    int sourceCol = source.getCol();
    int targetRow = target.getRow();
    int targetCol = target.getCol();

    // Check if move is along a straight line

        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}

Response Text:---
The `validate` method is designed to check if a move involving a Knight piece in chess is valid according to specific rules. Since the current implementation returns `true` if the piece at the source is not a Knight, and `false` otherwise, the student implementation should verify whether the move conforms to the Knight's movement pattern (an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular).

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method that checks if the move is a valid Knight move:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int targetRow = move.getTarget().getRow();
    int targetCol = move.getTarget().getCol();

    int rowDiff = Math.abs(targetRow - sourceRow);
    int colDiff = Math.abs(targetCol - sourceCol);

    // Knight moves: (2,1) or (1,2)
    return (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
}
```

This implementation calculates the differences in row and column between the source and target positions and confirms whether they match the Knight's movement pattern.

Response Text:---
The blocking rule for a Knight (or horse) in Chinese chess (Xiangqi) states that the Knight's movement can be blocked if the "leg" position (the position adjacent to the source in the direction of movement) is occupied. To implement this, we need to check the position that the Knight "steps over" when moving in an L-shape.

In the typical move, the Knight moves two steps in one direction and one step perpendicular. The "leg" position is the one adjacent to the source in the direction of the two-step move.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    int rowDiff = destRow - sourceRow;
    int colDiff = destCol - sourceCol;

    // Check for valid Knight move (L-shape)
    if (!((Math.abs(rowDiff) == 2 && Math.abs(colDiff) == 1) ||
          (Math.abs(rowDiff) == 1 && Math.abs(colDiff) == 2))) {
        return true; // Not a Knight move, so no blocking concern
    }

    // Determine the "leg" position that must be free
    int legRow = sourceRow + (rowDiff / Math.abs(rowDiff) == 0 ? 0 : rowDiff / Math.abs(rowDiff));
    int legCol = sourceCol + (colDiff / Math.abs(colDiff) == 0 ? 0 : colDiff / Math.abs(colDiff));

    // For the "leg" position, move one step in the direction of the two-step move
    if (Math.abs(rowDiff) == 2) {
        legRow = sourceRow + (rowDiff / 2);
        legCol = sourceCol;
    } else {
        legRow = sourceRow;
        legCol = sourceCol + (colDiff / 2);
    }

    // Check if the "leg" position is occupied
    Place legPosition = new Place(legRow, legCol);
    if (game.getPiece(legPosition) != null) {
        return false; // Blocked
    }

    return true; // Not blocked
}
```

**Explanation:**
- First, verify the move is an L-shape.
- Calculate the "leg" position based on the move direction.
- Check if the "leg" position is occupied.
- Return `false` if blocked; otherwise, `true`.

This implementation ensures the Knight's move respects the blocking rule in Chinese chess.

public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {

    return true;
}
```

package assignment.player;

import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.piece.*;
import assignment.protocol.Color;
import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Scanner;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
	public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
		super(name, color);
	}

	public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
		this(name, Color.GREEN);
	}

	/**
	 * Choose a move from available moves.
	 * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
	 * player's turn.
	 * <p>
	 * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
	 * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
	 * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */
	@Override
	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return availableMoves[0];
	}

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}
}

	@NotNull

		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();

```java
public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
    // Find the player's current position
    Position playerPosition = null;
    for (int row = 0; row < gameBoard.getNumRows(); row++) {
        for (int col = 0; col < gameBoard.getNumCols(); col++) {
            Position pos = new Position(row, col);
            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(pos);
            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
                if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Player) {
                    playerPosition = pos;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (playerPosition != null) {
            break;
        }
    }

    if (playerPosition == null) {
        // Player not found; no move possible
        return new MoveResult.Invalid(null);
    }

    // Simulate the move
    MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(playerPosition, direction);

    if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validResult) {
        // Check if the player is still alive after the move
        if (validResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveResult) {
            // Save current state for undo
            // (Assuming there's a way to save previous state, e.g., a stack or similar)
            // For simplicity, assume we have a method saveState() and restoreState()
            // saveState();

            // Mutate the game board: move the player
            // Remove player from old position
            gameBoard.setCell(playerPosition, new EmptyCell());
            // Place player at new position
            gameBoard.setCell(aliveResult.getNewPosition(), new EntityCell(new Player()));

            // Optionally, handle collected gems and extra lives
            // (Assuming gameBoard or Player handles inventory; omitted for brevity)

            return validResult;
        } else {
            // Player died; do not mutate the game board
            return validResult;
        }
    } else {
        // Invalid move; do nothing
        return moveResult;
    }
}

The `undoMove` method should revert the game state to what it was before the move represented by `prevMove`. This involves restoring the player's position, re-adding any collected gems or extra lives, and removing any entities (like mines or gems) that were collected during the move. Additionally, if the move resulted in the player dying, the method should restore the previous position and state accordingly.

Here's a brief explanation of how to implement it:

- Check if `prevMove` is valid.
- Retrieve the current position of the player.
- Restore the player's previous position.
- If the move was valid and the player was alive, move the player back to the previous position.
- If the move resulted in death, handle accordingly (e.g., restore the previous position and state).
- Re-add any collected gems or extra lives at their previous positions.
- Remove any entities that were collected during the move from the game board.

```java
public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    if (prevMove == null) {
        return;
    }

    // Find current player position
    Position currentPlayerPos = null;
    for (int row = 0; row < gameBoard.getNumRows(); row++) {
        for (int col = 0; col < gameBoard.getNumCols(); col++) {
            Position pos = new Position(row, col);
            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(pos);
            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell && entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Player) {
                currentPlayerPos = pos;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (currentPlayerPos != null) {
            break;
        }
    }

    // Determine previous position
    Position prevPosition;
    ArrayList<Position> prevGems = new ArrayList<>();
    ArrayList<Position> prevExtraLives = new ArrayList<>();

    if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
        prevPosition = validMove.getPreviousPosition();
        prevGems.addAll(validMove.getCollectedGems());
        prevExtraLives.addAll(validMove.getCollectedExtraLives());
    } else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Invalid invalidMove) {
        // No move was made; nothing to undo
        return;
    } else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead deadMove) {
        prevPosition = deadMove.getPreviousPosition();
        // No gems or extra lives collected if dead
    } else {
        // Unknown move result type
        return;
    }

    // Clear current player position
    if (currentPlayerPos != null) {
        gameBoard.setCell(currentPlayerPos, new EmptyCell());
    }

    // Restore previous position of the player
    gameBoard.setCell(prevPosition, new EntityCell(new Player()));

    // Re-add collected gems
    for (Position gemPos : prevGems) {
        gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EntityCell(new Gem()));
    }

    // Re-add collected extra lives
    for (Position lifePos : prevExtraLives) {
        gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EntityCell(new ExtraLife()));
    }
}

If these methods are named differently, adjust accordingly. Also, it handles restoring the player's position and re-adding collected items, effectively reversing the move.

package pa1.controller;

/**
 * Controller for {@link GameBoard}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class is responsible for providing high-level operations to mutate a {@link GameBoard}. This should be the only
 * class which mutates the game board; Other classes should use this class to mutate the game board.
 * </p>
 */
public class GameBoardController {

	@NotNull
	private final GameBoard gameBoard;

	/**
	 * Undoes a move by reverting all changes performed by the specified move.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.
	 */
	public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
		// TODO
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	public void GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard);
	}

	public MoveResult makeMove(final Direction direction) {
		Position playerPosition = null;
		for (int row = 0; row < gameBoard.getNumRows(); row++) {
			for (int col = 0; col < gameBoard.getNumCols(); col++) {
				Position pos = new Position(row, col);
				Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(pos);
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
					if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Player) {
						playerPosition = pos;
						break;
					}
				}
			}
			if (playerPosition != null) {
				break;
			}
		}
		if (playerPosition == null) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(null);
		}
		MoveResult moveResult = tryMove(playerPosition, direction);
		if (moveResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid validResult) {
			if (validResult instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Alive aliveResult) {
				gameBoard.setCell(playerPosition, new EmptyCell());
				gameBoard.setCell(aliveResult.getNewPosition(), new EntityCell(new Player()));
				return validResult;
			} else {
				return validResult;
			}
		} else {
			return moveResult;
		}
	}
}

public void undoMove(final MoveResult prevMove) {
    if (prevMove == null) {
        return;
    }

    // Find current player position
    Position currentPlayerPos = null;
    for (int row = 0; row < gameBoard.getNumRows(); row++) {
        for (int col = 0; col < gameBoard.getNumCols(); col++) {
            Position pos = new Position(row, col);
            Cell cell = gameBoard.getCell(pos);
            if (cell instanceof EntityCell entityCell && entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Player) {
                currentPlayerPos = pos;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (currentPlayerPos != null) {
            break;
        }
    }

    // Determine previous position and collected items
    Position prevPosition = null;
    ArrayList<Position> prevGems = new ArrayList<>();
    ArrayList<Position> prevExtraLives = new ArrayList<>();

    if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid validMove) {
        prevPosition = validMove.getPreviousPosition();
        prevGems.addAll(validMove.getCollectedGems());
        prevExtraLives.addAll(validMove.getCollectedExtraLives());
    } else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Valid.Dead deadMove) {
        prevPosition = deadMove.getPreviousPosition();
        // No gems or extra lives collected if dead
    } else if (prevMove instanceof MoveResult.Invalid) {
        // No move was made; nothing to undo
        return;
    } else {
        // Unknown move result type
        return;
    }

    // Clear current player position
    if (currentPlayerPos != null) {
        gameBoard.setCell(currentPlayerPos, new EmptyCell());
    }

    // Restore previous position of the player
    gameBoard.setCell(prevPosition, new EntityCell(new Player()));

    // Re-add collected gems
    for (Position gemPos : prevGems) {
        gameBoard.setCell(gemPos, new EntityCell(new Gem()));
    }

    // Re-add collected extra lives
    for (Position lifePos : prevExtraLives) {
        gameBoard.setCell(lifePos, new EntityCell(new ExtraLife()));
    }
}

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**

public abstract class Entity implements BoardElement {

The `setEntity` method needs to perform ownership transfer by updating the previous entity's owner, clearing the previous owner's reference to the entity, updating the new entity's owner, and updating the cell's entity reference. Here's a complete implementation:

```java
public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
    // Store the current entity to return later
    Entity previousEntity = this.entity;

    // If there is a current entity, unset its owner
    if (this.entity != null) {
        this.entity.setOwner(null);
        // Also, clear the owner of the previous entity's cell if needed
        // (Assuming Entity has a getOwner() method returning EntityCell)
        EntityCell previousOwnerCell = this.entity.getOwner();
        if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == this.entity) {
            previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
        }
    }

    // Set the new entity
    this.entity = newEntity;

    if (newEntity != null) {
        // Unset the new entity's previous owner cell if any
        EntityCell previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner.getEntity() == newEntity) {
            previousOwner.entity = null;
        }
        // Set the new entity's owner to this cell
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
    }

    return previousEntity;
}
```

It also ensures that ownership is properly transferred, previous references are cleared, and the method returns the previous entity as specified.

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		this.entity = initialEntity;
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (this.entity != null) {
			this.entity.setOwner(null);
			EntityCell previousOwnerCell = this.entity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == this.entity) {
				previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
			}
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		if (newEntity != null) {
			EntityCell previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner.getEntity() == newEntity) {
				previousOwner.entity = null;
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

Specifically, the code attempts to instantiate `EntityCell` with various parameter combinations such as `EntityCell(Position)`, `EntityCell(Position, Entity)`, `EntityCell(Position, Gem)`, `EntityCell(Position, Player)`, `EntityCell(Position, ExtraLife)`, `EntityCell(Position, Mine)`, etc., but these constructors are not found in the class definition.

**Explanation:**  
To fix these errors, you need to define all necessary constructors in the `EntityCell` class that match the usages in your code. For example, constructors like:

```java
public EntityCell(Position position) { ... }
public EntityCell(Position position, Entity entity) { ... }
public EntityCell(Position position, Gem gem) { ... }
public EntityCell(Position position, Player player) { ... }
public EntityCell(Position position, ExtraLife extraLife) { ... }
public EntityCell(Position position, Mine mine) { ... }
```

must be implemented in `EntityCell`. Without these, Java cannot instantiate `EntityCell` objects with those parameter combinations, leading to the compilation errors observed.

---

**Proposed fix:**

Add all relevant constructors to the `EntityCell` class, for example:

```java
public class EntityCell extends Cell {
    // existing fields and methods

    public EntityCell(Position position) {
        super(position);
        // initialize as needed
    }

    public EntityCell(Position position, Entity entity) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = entity;
        if (entity != null) {
            entity.setOwner(this);
        }
    }

    public EntityCell(Position position, Gem gem) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = gem;
        if (gem != null) {
            gem.setOwner(this);
        }
    }

    public EntityCell(Position position, Player player) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = player;
        if (player != null) {
            player.setOwner(this);
        }
    }

    public EntityCell(Position position, ExtraLife extraLife) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = extraLife;
        if (extraLife != null) {
            extraLife.setOwner(this);
        }
    }

    public EntityCell(Position position, Mine mine) {
        super(position);
        this.entity = mine;
        if (mine != null) {
            mine.setOwner(this);
        }
    }
}
```

Ensure that all constructors are properly implemented in `EntityCell`. This will allow the instantiation code in your tests and other classes to compile successfully.

**Note:**  
Since the project uses Java 19, make sure all constructors are public (or package-private if intended), and that the `Position`, `Entity`, `Gem`, `Player`, `ExtraLife`, and `Mine` classes are properly defined with their respective constructors and `setOwner` methods if needed.

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		this.entity = initialEntity;
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (this.entity != null) {
			this.entity.setOwner(null);
			EntityCell previousOwnerCell = this.entity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwnerCell != null && previousOwnerCell.getEntity() == this.entity) {
				previousOwnerCell.entity = null;
			}
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		if (newEntity != null) {
			EntityCell previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner.getEntity() == newEntity) {
				previousOwner.entity = null;
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

/**
 * The result after moving a player.
 */
public abstract class MoveResult {

	/**
	 * The {@link Position} of the player after moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	public final Position newPosition;

	/**
	 * Represents a valid move.
	 */
	public static class Valid extends MoveResult {

		/**
		 * The original position of the player before the move.
		 */
		@NotNull
		public final Position origPosition;

		/**
		 * Creates an instance of {@link Valid}, indicating that the move is valid.
		 *
		 * @param newPosition  The new {@link Position} of the player after moving.
		 * @param origPosition The original {@link Position} of the player before moving.
		 */
		private Valid(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition) {
			super(newPosition);

			this.origPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(origPosition);
		}

		/**
		 * Represents a valid move, and the player is alive after making the move.
		 */
		public static final class Alive extends Valid {

			/**
			 * List of positions representing the location of {@link Gem} collected in this move.
			 */
			@NotNull
			public final List<Position> collectedGems;
			/**
			 * List of positions representing the location of {@link ExtraLife} collected in this move.
			 */
			@NotNull
			public final List<Position> collectedExtraLives;

			/**
			 * Creates an instance of {@link Alive}, indicating that the move is valid and the player
			 * is still alive after the move.
			 *
			 * <p>
			 * {@link Alive#collectedGems} and {@link Alive#collectedExtraLives} will be initialized to an empty list
			 * using this constructor.
			 * </p>
			 *
			 * @param newPosition  The new {@link Position} of the player after the move.
			 * @param origPosition The original {@link Position} of the player before the move.
			 */
			public Alive(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition) {
				this(newPosition, origPosition, Collections.emptyList(), Collections.emptyList());
			}

			/**
			 * Creates an instance of {@link Alive}, indicating that the move is valid and the player
			 * is still alive after the move.
			 *
			 * @param newPosition         The new {@link Position} of the player after the move.
			 * @param origPosition        The original {@link Position} of the player before the move.
			 * @param collectedGems       The list of positions of all gems collected in this move.
			 * @param collectedExtraLives The list of positions of all extra lives collected in this move.
			 */
			public Alive(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition,
					@NotNull final List<Position> collectedGems, @NotNull final List<Position> collectedExtraLives) {
				super(newPosition, origPosition);

				this.collectedGems = Collections.unmodifiableList(Objects.requireNonNull(collectedGems));
				this.collectedExtraLives = Collections.unmodifiableList(Objects.requireNonNull(collectedExtraLives));
			}
		}

		/**

		public static final class Dead extends Valid {

It also assigns the validated data to the class fields.

Here's a complete implementation of the `GameBoard` constructor:

```java
public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
    // Validate dimensions
    if (cells.length != numRows) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of rows does not match cells array length");
    }
    if (cells.length == 0 || cells[0].length != numCols) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of columns does not match cells array width");
    }

    // Assign fields
    this.numRows = numRows;
    this.numCols = numCols;

    // Deep copy or assign the cells array
    this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];
    for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
        if (cells[r].length != numCols) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Row " + r + " length does not match numCols");
        }
        System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
    }

    // Verify exactly one player exists
    Player foundPlayer = null;
    int gemCount = 0;
    for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < numCols; c++) {
            Cell cell = this.board[r][c];
            if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec) {
                if (ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
                    if (foundPlayer != null) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("More than one player found");
                    }
                    foundPlayer = p;
                }
                if (ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                    gemCount++;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if (foundPlayer == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No player found");
    }

    if (gemCount == 0) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No gems found");
    }

    // Check reachability of all gems
    Position playerPos = ((EntityCell) getCell(foundPlayer.getOwner().getPosition())).getPosition();
    List<Position> reachablePositions = getAllReachablePositions(playerPos);
    int reachableGems = 0;
    for (Position pos : reachablePositions) {
        Cell cell = getCell(pos);
        if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
            reachableGems++;
        }
    }
    if (reachableGems != gemCount) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems are unreachable");
    }

    // Assign the player instance
    this.player = foundPlayer;
}
```

**Note:**  
- This implementation assumes that `getCell(Position)` and `getCell(int, int)` are properly implemented to retrieve cells from `board`.  
- It also assumes that `Player` has a method `getOwner()` returning a `Position`. If not, you should adjust accordingly.  
- The constructor performs all necessary validation and initializes the class fields to ensure the `GameBoard` instance is correctly set up.
